title: Claude Model History
content:
## Overview

Claude is Anthropic's family of AI assistants, first released in early 2023. Each generation has brought meaningful jumps in capability, context length, and cost-efficiency. This page tracks the major releases and what changed with each one.

---

## Claude 1 (March 2023)

The first publicly available Claude, launched via API and the Claude.ai interface. Introduced Anthropic's "Constitutional AI" approach to alignment — training the model to critique and revise its own outputs against a set of principles rather than relying solely on human feedback (RLHF).

**Key specs:** ~9K token context window, text-only input.

---

## Claude 2 (July 2023)

A major capability jump. Notable improvements in coding, math, and instruction following. Introduced a **100K token context window** — at the time one of the largest available, enabling entire codebases or books to fit in a single prompt.

**Key specs:** 100K context, text-only input, improved reasoning benchmarks.

---

## Claude 2.1 (November 2023)

Expanded context to **200K tokens** and significantly reduced hallucination rates on long-document tasks. Also introduced system prompt support and improved tool use.

---

## Claude 3 Family (March 2024)

Anthropic introduced a three-tier model family with a consistent naming convention that persists today:

- **Haiku** — fastest, cheapest, suitable for high-throughput applications
- **Sonnet** — balanced capability and cost, the default workhorse
- **Opus** — most capable, used for complex reasoning tasks

All Claude 3 models gained **vision (image input)** support, enabling document analysis, chart reading, and screenshot processing. Context window: 200K tokens across all tiers.

**Claude 3 Opus** set new benchmarks on MMLU, HumanEval, and GSM8K at launch.

---

## Claude 3.5 Sonnet (June 2024)

A landmark release: **Claude 3.5 Sonnet outperformed Claude 3 Opus on most benchmarks while being significantly faster and cheaper**. This broke the usual pattern where the top-tier model leads on capability.

Also introduced **Artifacts** in Claude.ai — the ability to generate self-contained code, documents, and interactive apps displayed in a side panel.

---

## Claude 3.5 Sonnet v2 / Computer Use (October 2024)

Updated Claude 3.5 Sonnet with improved coding and a major new capability: **computer use (beta)** — the ability to control a computer by seeing the screen and issuing mouse/keyboard actions. Made available via API for developers to build agentic desktop automation.

---

## Claude 3.5 Haiku (November 2024)

The fastest and most affordable Claude 3.5 model. Matched or exceeded Claude 3 Opus on several benchmarks despite being positioned as the lightweight tier.

---

## Claude 4 Family (2025)

Continuing the Haiku / Sonnet / Opus naming, this generation ran through most of 2025. Model IDs from that period:

| Model | ID | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Haiku 4.5 | `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` | Fastest/cheapest Claude 4 |
| Sonnet 4.5 | `claude-sonnet-4-5` | Balanced |
| Sonnet 4.6 | `claude-sonnet-4-6` | Default Sonnet through mid-2026 |
| Opus 4.7 | `claude-opus-4-7` | Most capable of the 4.x line until Opus 4.8 |

Claude 4 models show substantial improvements in agentic task completion, long multi-turn coherence, and instruction following precision. All four models above were superseded by the releases below but remain available via the API.

---

## Claude Opus 4.8 (May 28, 2026)

A reliability-focused upgrade to Opus rather than a new tier — shipped at the same price as Opus 4.7 across the API, Bedrock, Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry. The headline improvements were about **honesty and self-assessment**, not just raw capability:

- ~4x less likely than Opus 4.7 to let flaws in its own generated code pass without flagging them
- Overconfidence down roughly 10x versus 4.7
- Misaligned-behavior score improved from ~2.5 to ~1.8 on Anthropic's internal 1–10 scale

Capability also moved: SWE-bench Pro rose from 64.3% to 69.2%, USAMO 2026 math score jumped from 69.3% to 96.7%, and long-context tracking (GraphWalks at 1M tokens) nearly doubled from 40.3% to 68.1%.

---

## Claude Fable 5 & Claude Mythos 5 — The Mythos Tier (June 9, 2026)

Anthropic introduced a new tier **above Opus**, called **Mythos class** — the most capable models Anthropic has released publicly. Two models shipped together:

- **Claude Fable 5** — the public-facing Mythos-class model, with safety classifiers that can decline requests
- **Claude Mythos 5** — same underlying capability as Fable 5 but without those safety classifiers; available only through limited release ( **Project Glasswing** ) under a 30-day data retention policy for safety monitoring

Both launched alongside the US Department of Commerce lifting export restrictions that had previously blocked international access to these models.

**Specs:** 1M-token context window by default, up to 128K output tokens per request, priced at $10/$50 per million input/output tokens.

**Capability:** Mythos 5 scores 80.3% on SWE-bench Pro (vs. 69.2% for Opus 4.8) and Anthropic describes it as having the strongest cybersecurity capabilities of any model it has released, including agentic hacking across reconnaissance, vulnerability discovery, exploit-chain creation, and lateral movement — reflecting its design for high-autonomy agentic use with reduced human oversight.

---

## Claude Sonnet 5 (June 30, 2026)

The current default Sonnet, and default model for every Free and Pro user starting July 1, 2026. Positioned as the most agentic Sonnet yet, closing much of the gap to Opus 4.8 while staying mid-tier priced.

**Specs:** native 1M-token context window with context compaction; adaptive thinking with selectable effort levels up to `xhigh`. Introductory pricing of $2/$10 per million input/output tokens through August 31, 2026, rising to $3/$15 afterward. Note: Sonnet 5's tokenizer produces ~1.0–1.35x more tokens than Sonnet 4.6 for the same input text, so per-task cost can rise even at flat per-token rates.

**Benchmarks:** SWE-bench Verified 85.2%, SWE-bench Pro 63.2%, Terminal-Bench 2.1 80.4% (beating Opus 4.8's 74.6% — the first time a mid-tier Sonnet has beaten its own Opus sibling on a major coding benchmark), OSWorld-Verified 81.2%, USAMO 2026 79.5%.

---

## Key Trends Across Generations

- **Context window:** 9K → 100K → 200K → 1M tokens (Sonnet 5 and Fable/Mythos 5 both ship with native 1M windows)
- **Multimodal:** Text-only → Vision → Computer use
- **Tier structure:** Single model → Three tiers (Haiku / Sonnet / Opus) → Four tiers with the addition of Mythos class above Opus
- **Cost curve:** Each generation brings the previous generation's top-tier capability down to mid-tier pricing — Sonnet 5 approaching Opus 4.8 performance is the latest example
- **Agentic focus:** Increasing emphasis on tool use, long-horizon tasks, autonomous operation with reduced oversight, and integration with external systems
- **Trust, not just capability:** Opus 4.8 marks a shift toward explicitly measuring and improving honesty/self-assessment alongside raw benchmark scores
